# agency sections — catalog

<!-- Generated by `npm run index` from component headers. Do not edit by hand. -->

Pick by USE WHEN, then read only the chosen file. Follow ../DIRECTION.md exactly.

- **awards-line.tsx** — Recognition worth stating once — a quiet divide-y index of juried awards (tabular year, award, project). Plain text only: no badges, no laurel logos, no trust-spam strip. Reads like a colophon, not a trophy case.
- **capabilities-list.tsx** — Naming what the studio actually does — five numbered rows with oversized muted numbers and one plain line each. An index, not a card grid.
- **careers-band.tsx** — Hiring honestly — a bordered band with "We hire slowly.", one or two openings as divide-y rows (role, discipline, location), and a mailto for everyone else. Deliberately quiet: no cobalt anywhere except the hover underline.
- **case-study-feature.tsx** — One case deserves the whole stage — full-bleed image, then an asymmetric split: big result statement left, factual Client/Scope/Year/Result list right.
- **client-ticker.tsx** — A one-row strip of client names scrolling under the hero — social proof as typography, never a logo wall (the agency direction bans logo grids).
- **contact-cta.tsx** — The page closer — one big Syne question, a cobalt button, an underlined email, and an honest response-time line. Statement left, actions offset right.
- **culture-band.tsx** — Saying how the studio actually works — one Syne pull-line, two or three short Manrope paragraphs offset right (small teams, no account layer, everyone makes), and an optional wide studio photo. No headshots — team-grid.tsx has those.
- **hero-manifesto.tsx** — The agency landing page opener — a point-of-view statement, not a service list. Headline runs two-thirds wide with the supporting copy offset right.
- **journal-teaser.tsx** — Surfacing three recent opinions as an index — divide-y rows, whole row a link, title takes a cobalt underline on hover. Proof the studio has a point of view.
- **process-steps.tsx** — Explaining how engagements actually run — three phases with oversized cobalt numbers, honest timeframes, and thin rules. Heading left, phases right (two-thirds).
- **services-detail.tsx** — A capabilities page needs depth, not an index — three disciplines as asymmetric blocks that stagger across the grid: Syne subhead, a short Manrope paragraph, and a "Recent:" line linking a real case. The deeper alternative to capabilities-list.tsx; never run both on the same page.
- **team-grid.tsx** — Showing the crew candidly — five photo slots at varying sizes and offsets (never a uniform headshot wall), names + roles, one collective caption.
- **work-showcase.tsx** — The main work grid — five case tiles in an asymmetric layout with one-line factual results. Each tile is a link; the name takes a cobalt underline on hover.
